primary.title: How SQM Turned a 678 km² Mine into an Autonomous Inspection Zone
primary.why_strongest_fit: This case study is about the lead's own company. It describes SQM running DJI Dock-based drones on FlytBase across its 678 km² mining operation in the Atacama Desert, which is the same desert, the same type of operation and the same autonomous-inspection use case Rodrigo Castillo is asking about. It shows autonomy replacing manual field inspections (engineers walking or driving kilometers each day), which matches his complaint about expensive, hazardous inspection crews. It also proves FlytBase works in SQM's environment, with its IT stack (Azure integration) and through a local Chile-based partner (Adentu). So the open question is no longer whether this works at SQM. It becomes how to extend it to the Northern Operations lithium sites. No other case study can match that level of specificity.
key_proof_points: SQM cut inspection time from days to hours
achieved more than 95 percent mission reliability
improved iodine extraction yield by two percent (the page headline separately says '4× iodine yield improvement'; confirm which figure to quote)
678 km² mining operation in northern Chile (Atacama Desert)
"Every hour our engineers spent walking was an hour not solving the problem" - Rodrigo Toler, Deputy Manager of Digital Innovation, SQM
"The FlytBase platform let us automate daily missions, health checks, and data transfers, building a truly hands-free workflow" - José Pablo Mujica, Commercial Manager, Adentu
primary.how_to_use_it: Open by acknowledging that SQM's innovation team already runs FlytBase autonomy with Adentu in the Atacama. Do not pitch as if SQM were a new logo. Position the conversation as scaling a proven internal program to Rodrigo Castillo's 3 lithium sites with 24/7 coverage. Quote the days-to-hours, >95% reliability and 2x frequency figures and attach the case study. Ask whether he has spoken with Rodrigo Toler's digital innovation team. Coordinate with Adentu before outreach to avoid channel conflict. Use the Anglo American case (S2) as the referral bridge.

secondary.title: How Anglo American Uses Autonomous Drones to Transform Mining Safety in Peru
secondary.why: This is the referrer's own FlytBase deployment. Drone-in-a-box at the Quellaveco copper mine in Peru with partner UAV LATAM replaced manual drone flights and truck travel between survey points and reduced personnel exposure to hazards in harsh LATAM mining terrain. It validates the referral and directly supports Castillo's safety and crew-cost pain points. Use it to name-check Anglo American credibly in the first email.

referral_connection.explanation: FlytBase's site has a published case study on Anglo American, the referrer named in the email. It covers autonomous drone-in-a-box operations at the Quellaveco copper mine in Peru, powered by FlytBase and implemented with partner UAV LATAM. It replaced manual Mavic Air flights and truck travel between survey points, and used docks on elevated positions for communication in mountainous terrain. This explains how Anglo American knows FlytBase and why it would refer another LATAM miner.

existing_relationship.explanation: Yes. SQM is already a FlytBase customer according to FlytBase's own case study. SQM's innovation team partnered with Adentu, a Chile-based integrator, and FlytBase to run DJI Dock-based autonomous inspections (RGB and thermal) across its 678 km² Atacama operation, with data relayed to SQM's Azure environment for ML analysis. The work started as a pilot on irrigation leaks and leaching inefficiencies (one dock, one zone) and became a fully automated inspection ecosystem. Reported results: inspection time cut from days to hours, >95% mission reliability, doubled inspection frequency and a 2% iodine extraction yield improvement. The inbound comes from a different part of SQM (Northern Operations, lithium extraction), so this is an expansion opportunity with an incumbent partner (Adentu) to coordinate with.
